name: Stop and target given as percentages become real prices
why: The owner's real note. Traders quote risk off the entry ("stop 0.5% lower, target 1%") rather than as absolute levels; deriving them from a stated entry is arithmetic on what was said, not invention, and leaving them null would mean retyping both. NOTE: "62.975" is genuinely ambiguous — the model has returned both 62.975 (literal) and 62975 (read as $62,975, the realistic BTC price) across runs. That is an open product decision, so this fixture deliberately does not assert the entry price; it asserts the parts that are stable.
